clue.text: Riches from rough grazing ? No Rex

definitions.note: Rex is Latin for king; a state with no king is a republic or commonwealth

parts.note: a common is open, unfenced land where villagers may graze animals
riches are wealth

explanation.surface: A farmer hoping for a fortune from scrubby pasture, with no royal involvement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No Rex' is the definition: a state governed without a king, as England was under Cromwell.
explanation.definitionFit: A state run for the common good without a monarch is called by this name, as in Cromwell's republic.

clue.text: All present are firm

definitions.meaning: everyone gathered together in a room forms the party or group
a business, as in a limited liability concern

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: the people assembled around you, and a business enterprise or corporation.

clue.text: Pegasus ? He would !

parts.note: Pegasus is a horse, something ridden, and the exclamation says a rider would climb on to it

explanation.definitionFit: Pegasus, the winged horse of Greek myth, is a steed to ride, and a hero would climb onto it.

clue.text: Ancient town of Germany

parts.note: olden means of former days, ancient
Burg is a German word for a fortified town, as in many German place names

explanation.surface: A plain gazetteer entry for an old German settlement.
explanation.definitionFit: Oldenburg is a historic city in Lower Saxony, northern Germany.

clue.text: Prosperity as a mark of punishment

definitions.meaning: an old sense of the word, as in the common good or well-being
a red ridge raised on the skin by a whip or cane

explanation.definitionFit: Archaic word for well-being, and also a raised welt left by a lash.

clue.text: Pain-soother, note, for the ambitious

parts.note: aspirin is a common painkiller
G is one of the musical notes A to G

explanation.surface: A doctor recommends a painkiller and a memo for go-getters.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone ambitious is striving upward toward a goal.

clue.text: A woman despite being a good artist

parts.note: tho is a short spelling of though, meaning despite that
RA, a Royal Academician, is a distinguished artist

explanation.surface: A woman described with surprise as both female and a fine painter.
explanation.walkthrough: RA stands for Royal Academician, an elected member of Britain's Royal Academy of Arts.
explanation.definitionFit: Thora is a female given name, as with the actress Thora Hird.

clue.text: Old crone, right leg's broken. They argue what should be paid

definitions.text: They argue what should be paid

parts.note: a hag is an ugly old woman

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so these letters are reassembled in a new order

parts.note: the word leg's supplies its letters as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: An old woman's leg is broken; then a dispute over a bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges R and LEGS into GLERS, which follows HAG.
explanation.definitionFit: Bargainers dispute a price, arguing over how much money changes hands.

clue.text: Obvious what the inventor's after

definitions.meaning: plain to see, as in a clear lie
an inventor seeks official protection of the rights to a new device

explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means plain or evident; as a noun it is the legal right an inventor applies for.

clue.text: Underground worker has to fashion threads for weavers

parts.note: to mould something is to shape or fashion it
the warp is the set of lengthwise threads on a loom

explanation.surface: A miner who also makes the yarn used by textile workers.
explanation.walkthrough: The underground worker is a mole, for which this is an old dialect name.
explanation.definitionFit: An old country name for the mole, a burrowing animal that tunnels through soil.

clue.text: Twisted oaks with a Japanese build-up

indicators.note: twisted means bent out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Gnarled oak trees growing in a Japanese setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twisted' rearranges OAKS into OSAK, then A is added. 'build-up' stands for a built-up area, a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Osaka is a major Japanese city, a large urban sprawl.

clue.text: Show 15 in " Death of a Pussyfoot "

indicators.note: the end of something follows it, so this piece comes after the others

parts.note: a teetotaller, after the American prohibitionist William 'Pussyfoot' Johnson; TT means teetotal
death is the end of life

explanation.surface: Advice to show interest in a play called Death of a Pussyfoot.
explanation.walkthrough: 15 is INTEREST, so the definition reads 'show interest in'. 'of' puts the death (END) after A TT.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay heed to something or be present at it is to show concern for it.

clue.text: Euclidean percussion

definitions.meaning: a three-sided figure from Euclid's geometry
a metal instrument struck with a rod in an orchestra

explanation.definitionFit: A three-sided plane figure of geometry, and a steel percussion instrument bent into that shape.

clue.text: Lip-smacking girl in kimono

definitions.meaning: an exclamation of delight at tasty food
a heroine of Gilbert and Sullivan's comic opera The Mikado, set in Japan

explanation.definitionFit: A childish cry of relish for delicious food, and the young ward of Ko-Ko in The Mikado.

clue.text: Like the day that's out of joint

definitions.text: Like the day that's out of joint

parts.words: Like the day that's out of joint
parts.note: out of joint reads as having no roast joint, a day when no flesh is eaten

explanation.definitionFit: A day without flesh food, such as a Friday of abstinence, has no roast on the table.

clue.text: The percentage is a matter of concern

definitions.meaning: the rate a lender charges on a loan
something one cares about

explanation.definitionFit: The charge paid on borrowed money, and something that holds one's attention or concern.

clue.text: What's up with architecture ?

parts.note: what's up means height above, and in architecture it is also a drawing of a building's face

explanation.definitionFit: Height above a level, and in architecture a flat drawing of one face of a building.

clue.text: Advertisement in The Motor places it in Switzerland

indicators.note: the ad is placed inside the word for the motor

parts.note: an engine is a motor

explanation.surface: A car advert in The Motor magazine featuring Swiss locations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'places' links: the wordplay places the answer ('it') in Switzerland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Engadine is an Alpine valley of the Inn in Graubünden, eastern Switzerland.

clue.text: Like the clanger of a blueprint boffin ?

parts.note: a blueprint is a plan
the boffin is taken loosely as a gent, a fellow

explanation.surface: A scientist's design for a bell clapper.
explanation.walkthrough: The clanger is a bell's clapper, whose sound is resonant; the 'blueprint boffin' is a plan gent.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep resonant ring is how a bell's striker makes it sound.

clue.text: Glib talk of rain ? Hark

definitions.meaning: a salesman's smooth spiel
the light tapping sound raindrops make

explanation.definitionFit: A salesman's slick spiel, and the rapid light tapping of raindrops.

clue.text: Pestered when wanting a nap

definitions.meaning: annoyed or mocked
cloth is combed with teasels to raise a soft surface pile

explanation.definitionFit: Annoyed by mockery, and of cloth, brushed with teasels to raise its pile.

clue.text: So long a pair of shorts go to the feet

definitions.text: So long a pair of shorts go to the feet

parts.words: So long a pair of shorts go to the feet
parts.note: in verse, one long syllable then two short ones make up a metrical foot

explanation.definitionFit: Metrical feet of one stressed or long syllable followed by two unstressed ones, as in 'merrily'.

clue.text: Wire for dairy substitute allowed back

indicators.note: back means the joined words are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: marge is short for margarine, a butter substitute
let means allowed

explanation.surface: A message requesting margarine because butter is now permitted again.
explanation.definitionFit: A wire is an old informal word for a cabled message sent by telegraph.

clue.text: In Greek, one who is ruined

indicators.note: one sits inside the abbreviation for Greek

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tragic figure in a Greek drama is brought down.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition 'who is ruined' leans on 'one' to read 'one who is ruined'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone done for, beyond hope, is a person past saving.

clue.text: (Exclude most of Falstaff's) wine

parts.note: to bar is to exclude

indicators.note: most of means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: sack, a dry white wine, is the favourite drink of Shakespeare's Falstaff

explanation.surface: A note to leave out much of Falstaff's drinking, followed by wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims SACK to SAC. Falstaff is Shakespeare's fat knight, famously fond of sack.
explanation.definitionFit: Barsac is a sweet white wine from Bordeaux.

clue.text: Somewhat soothing, this greeting.

definitions.meaning: an ointment, something that eases pain
Latin for hail, a word of welcome

explanation.definitionFit: A soothing ointment, and the Latin word of greeting meaning 'hail' or 'be well'.

clue.text: Breeze in to lunch

definitions.meaning: a breeze is a minor quarrel or squabble
an Anglo-Indian verb, to take the midday meal, as in tiffin

explanation.definitionFit: A petty quarrel (a breeze in old slang), and in Anglo-Indian use, to take a light midday meal.

clue.text: He's sent to banish high tension in the Ruhr

indicators.note: banishing sends these letters out of the words

parts.note: the letters of these words as written, without the apostrophe
HT is the abbreviation for high tension in electrics

explanation.surface: A man is despatched to get rid of high-voltage cables in the industrial Ruhr.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to banish' removes the H and the T from HESSENT, leaving the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Essen is a major industrial city of the Ruhr district in western Germany.

clue.text: By using nominal capital at first?

definitions.meaning: by means of the capital letters starting a name
at the beginning

explanation.definitionFit: By means of a name's first letters, and at the outset or to begin with.

clue.text: Clever grafters never caught red-handed

parts.note: grafters are gardeners grafting plants; their hands are a different colour from guilty red

explanation.definitionFit: A gift for making plants grow is called by this colourful phrase.
